memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: evaluation of allergic rhinitis and benign prostatic hyperplasia.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: The patient reports year‑round nasal congestion, clear rhinorrhea, sneezing, and mild ocular itching. He also notes increased nocturia (2‑3 times/night) and a weak urinary stream over the past 6 months.
EXAMINATION: Vital signs: BP 138/86 mmHg, pulse 78/min. Weight 78 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 27.6 (obese). Nasal mucosa pale and boggy. Prostate not enlarged on digital rectal exam; no palpable nodules.
IMPRESSION: 1. Allergic rhinitis, likely perennial. 2. Benign prostatic hyperplasia, symptomatic. 3. Obesity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start cetirizine 10 mg HS, fluticasone nasal spray one spray each nostril OD, montelukast 10 mg HS for AR. Start tamsulosin 0.4 mg HS and finasteride 5 mg OD for BPH. Advise low‑calorie diet, 150 min/week brisk walking, and weight monitoring. Return if: worsening nasal obstruction with purulent discharge, fever >39°C, hematuria, acute urinary retention, or chest pain.

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I’ve been sneezing a lot in the mornings and my nose feels blocked. At night I wake up to pass urine two or three times, which is troubling me.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Follow‑up appointment booked for 2025-07-10 at 10:30 am with Dr Priya Natarajan.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up of allergic rhinitis and BPH.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says nasal symptoms are much better; occasional sneezing only on dusty days. Nocturia reduced to once per night; stream feels stronger.
EXAMINATION: BP 132/80 mmHg. Weight 77 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 27.3 (obese). Nasal mucosa mildly erythematous, no polyps. Prostate still not markedly enlarged on exam.
IMPRESSION: Allergic rhinitis well controlled. BPH symptomatic improvement. Obesity persists.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current AR meds. Reduce tamsulosin to 0.2 mg HS (considering symptom relief). Keep finasteride 5 mg OD. Reinforce diet and activity; aim for 5 kg weight loss over 3 months. Return if: nasal discharge becomes purulent, fever >39°C, worsening urinary retention, hematuria, or chest pain.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: annual review and preventive care.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports stable allergic rhinitis symptoms; occasional mild nasal itching. No urinary bother; nocturia absent.
EXAMINATION: BP 128/78 mmHg. Weight 75 kg, height 1.68 m, BMI 26.6 (overweight). Nasal mucosa normal. Prostate benign on exam.
IMPRESSION: Allergic rhinitis controlled. BPH symptoms resolved. Overweight per Asian cut‑offs; advise diet and exercise. Annual lipid and glucose checked.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue cetirizine, fluticasone, montelukast, tamsulosin, finasteride. Offer influenza vaccine (patient >60 with chronic AR) – administered today 02‑Oct‑2025. Reinforce weight goal of 70 kg. Return if: fever >39°C, shortness of breath, chest pain, hematuria, or sudden worsening of nasal blockage.
